member.name: T:DotNetCore.HayateOP.ObjectPoolCompat.HayateCompatPooledObjectPolicy`1
member.summary: Adapts the Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool to HayateOP's so that existing policy implementations drive HayateOP pools unchanged.
member.remarks:
Hook mapping (MEOP has only two hooks; the rest map to no-ops):
Create() →
OnRelease(item) → (returning false rejects the object, which HayateOP destroys — consistent with the MEOP "discard" semantics)
Validate → always true (MEOP has no borrow-time validation; IResettable.TryReset is handled internally by the default MEOP policy and naturally reaches the Return hook)
OnAcquire/OnPassivate/OnDestroy → no-op

member.name: P:DotNetCore.HayateOP.ObjectPoolCompat.HayateCompatOptions.MinSize
member.summary: Pre-warm count. Defaults to 0 (MEOP DefaultObjectPool also lazily creates). Pre-warming is now purely a warm-up optimisation: a pool below capacity creates synchronously on a miss, so a cold pool no longer pays a borrow delay (see ).

member.name: P:DotNetCore.HayateOP.ObjectPoolCompat.HayateCompatOptions.MaxSize
member.summary: Capacity upper bound. Defaults to Environment.ProcessorCount * 2, aligning with the default maximumRetained of MEOP DefaultObjectPool.

member.name: P:DotNetCore.HayateOP.ObjectPoolCompat.HayateCompatOptions.AcquireTimeout
member.summary: Borrow timeout for a request that finds no idle object. Defaults to 1s. It bounds only the one case the pool cannot serve by creating: every capacity slot is already taken and every object is lent out. A miss below — including the very first borrow of a cold pool — creates synchronously and returns immediately, so this value is not part of the cold-start path.
